title: They tunneled into a bank vault from the sewers and vanished with 50 million francs
description:
July 16, 1976. A bank manager in Nice opens the vault at Société Générale and finds a hole in the wall. Not a crack — a tunnel, eight meters long, carved from the city sewer straight into the steel-lined vault. Over the Bastille Day weekend, someone emptied 273 safe deposit boxes and walked out with 50 million francs. No alarm. No witnesses. No fingerprints — every surface wiped clean. The tunnel was engineering. Timber-shored.

Ventilated with an electric fan. They'd been digging for weeks beneath Avenue Jean Médecin. Police found a thermos, a handful of tools, one rubber glove. That was it. Here's where it broke. The sewer had maps. Access points had locks. Someone knew the grade, the turns, the exact distance to the vault's west wall. Every sewer worker in Nice was questioned and cleared.

Every single one. Forensics matched nothing. Interpol flagged nothing. The 50 million francs never surfaced — not one note. The thermos still had coffee in it. DNA didn't exist in 1976. The glove was sold at 200 shops across France. Forty-eight years later, it remains the largest unsolved bank robbery in French history. The tunnel was sealed with concrete. The coffee was never tested.
